title: Add Blossom server compliance test suite
body:
## Summary

- Adds a comprehensive compliance test suite covering **BUD-00 through BUD-12**, validating Blossom server implementations against the BUD specifications
- Each BUD has its own test module (`bud-XX.test.ts`) with both mandatory and optional behavior checks
- Includes an HTML + JSON report generator (`report.ts`) with per-server and per-BUD breakdowns

## What's included

**Test modules** (`bud-00.test.ts` – `bud-12.test.ts`):
- BUD-00: Server reachability
- BUD-01: Server requirements (CORS, error responses, blob retrieval, HEAD, range requests)
- BUD-02: Blob upload (PUT /upload, descriptors, X-SHA-256, duplicate handling)
- BUD-03: Skipped (client-side only, no server endpoints)
- BUD-04: Blob mirror (PUT /mirror, descriptor validation, error cases)
- BUD-05: Blob delete (DELETE /<sha256>, authorization)
- BUD-06: Blob upload (media) (PUT /media)
- BUD-07: Blob list (GET /list/<pubkey>)
- BUD-08: Blob TTL (upload with expiry)
- BUD-09: Blob report (PUT /report with kind:1984 events)
- BUD-10: Skipped (client-side only)
- BUD-11: Auth tokens (kind:24242, header validation)
- BUD-12: Identical blob deduplication

**Helpers** (`helpers/`):
- `http.ts` — HTTP request wrapper with auto-retry on 401 (detects auth-required servers)
- `nostr.ts` — Key pair generation, kind:24242 auth event building, base64url encoding
- `crypto.ts` — SHA-256 hashing, random bytes/blobs
- `assert.ts` — Assertion framework with pass/fail/warn/skip states
- `cleanup.ts` — Tracks and deletes uploaded blobs after each test run
- `test-blob.ts` — Generates unique PNG test images with Blossom branding
- `config.ts` — Server URL configuration via `BLOSSOM_SERVER_URL` env var

**Report generator** (`report.ts`):
- Runs all BUD tests against one or multiple servers
- Outputs `results.json` and styled `index.html` with pass/fail/warn breakdowns

## Usage

```bash
cd compliance-test
bun install

# Test a single server
BLOSSOM_SERVER_URL=https://your-server.com bun run report.ts

# Or import individual test modules
BLOSSOM_SERVER_URL=https://your-server.com bun test
```

title: BUD-12: Identical Media Deduplication
body:
## Summary

- Adds BUD-12, a new optional spec for servers to detect and reject uploads of media identical to an already-stored blob
- Servers respond with `409 Conflict` and an `X-Identical-Media: <sha256>` header pointing to the existing equivalent blob
- Detection method is left entirely to the server implementation (perceptual hashing, normalized hash, ML embeddings, etc.)
- Clients receiving the response should use the returned hash as the canonical reference and mirror it to other servers via BUD-04 rather than re-uploading
- Fully backwards compatible: clients that don't implement BUD-12 simply see a `409` upload failure

title: Usage of X-SHA-256 and other cleanups in BUD-11
body:
Hey @hzrd149, I found several issues in the current BUD-11, so instead of pointing them out I fixed them in a PR to the branch.

[Readable version](https://github.com/pippellia-btc/blossom-protocol/blob/update-auth-tokens/buds/11.md)

TLDR;

1. BUD-11 had a section "Endpoint-specific requirements" which didn't match the requirements in the specific BUDs. So I've unified all logic in the BUD-11, and other buds just link to it, which IMO makes implementations easier to make.

2. Previously, the "x" tag of an auth token of an /upload needed to match the request sha256. This is problematic because servers need to A) buffer the blob and B) compute the hash just to validate auth.  
We thought of using the `Content-Digest` header for this, however, that header has a specified encoding, which allows different hash functions. This freedom doesn't exists in blossom, so I preferred to use another header, which is `X-SHA-256`, already used in the HEAD /upload and HEAD /media.

I fixed also several typos, clarified few concepts, defined the encoding of `X-SHA-256`.
I've kept the requirement of the "x" tag for most endpoints, with the exception of GET /sha and HEAD /sha (even though I disagree and I would make it optional everywhere).

Take your time and let me know what you think.

title: Clarifying Auth
body:
This PR aims to clarity auth.

## Authentication vs Authorization

First, it renames Authorization events to Authentication events because:
1. The event is used by the Server to identify the Client with a Nostr pubkey, but has nothing to do with whether the Client is allowed to perform that action.
2. It aligns with the [NIP-42](https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/42.md)

I think NIP-98 is also wrong so I'll make a PR there as well (after hearing feedback here).

| /                 | Authentication | Authorization |
| -------------- | ---------------------  | -------------------- |
| Question  | Who are you?    | Are you allowed? |
| Specificity | Protocol specific | Implementation specific |

## Server URL Commitment

@hzrd149, as far as I've read the `GET /<sha256>` authentication flow is the only one that CAN accept a server tag containing the full server URL.

> The event MUST contain either a server tag containing the full URL to the server or MUST contain at least one x tag matching the sha256 hash of the blob being retrieved

This is in contrast to a previous paragraph

> Authorization events must be generic and must NOT be scoped to specific servers. This allows pubkeys to sign a single event and interact the same way with multiple servers.

I think the protocol should choose between always requiring the full URL like NIP-42 and NIP-98, or avoid it altogether.
I think the best way would be to always require the url, even though this comes at the cost of the client having to sign more events.

The reason is to have stronger authentication guarantees.
Let's consider this example:

- Alice sends a `DELETE /sha256` to Server A. She doesn't want Server A to host her blob anymore.
- The request correctly contains the Authentication event signed by Alice's key.
- Server A is malicious. Before event expiration, the server impersonates Alice with the blossom servers in her nostr list, and deletes her blob from all.

The benefits to using a custom `blossom:` URI vs the existing `http://<server>/<sha256>[.ext]` URL
 - File extension is required
 - Optional blob size parameter 
 - May include multiple server hints
 - May include multiple author hints that can be used with BUD-03 to discover live servers
 - Clients must parse the URI and implement some form of server fallback
 
 The downside to using a custom URI
  - Clients must implement more logic to parse the URI and handle server fallback

### BUD-07 Paid upload and download

This pull request introduces `BUD-07`, a new specification outlining how servers can require and handle payments for blob storage. It defines the use of `402 Payment Required` responses, with payment details provided via `X-{payment_method}` headers adhering to method-specific standards like **Cashu (NIP-18)** and **Lightning (BOLT-11)**.

The specification is **designed to be extensible** for future payment methods and includes guidance on client-server interactions.

title: Clarify has blob endpoint in BUD-01
body:
This PR adds more clarification about how the `HEAD /<sha256>` endpoint should behave along with requiring it to return the same headers that the `GET /<sha256>` endpoint returns.

[RFC 7231](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7231#section-4.3.2) only states that:

> The server SHOULD send the same
> header fields in response to a HEAD request as it would have sent if
> the request had been a GET, except that the payload header fields
> ([Section 3.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7231#section-3.3)) MAY be omitted.

I'm undecided if changing this from a SHOULD / MAY to a MUST is a good since it rules out simple servers that just want to respond with a `200` or `404` for checking if a blob exists. on the other hand it will make getting the blobs metadata ( `Content-Length` and `Content-Type` ) from the server easier for servers that do implement it


Fixes #45

title: BUD-06 Upload requirements
body:
This pull request introduces **BUD-06**, designed to define how clients can verify **upload requirements** before sending a blob to the server. This mechanism is intended to optimize performance by reducing unnecessary data transfers and providing clear error messages when uploads cannot proceed.

Readable version [here](https://github.com/hzrd149/blossom/blob/8e633d00b9394dc200bac3ec2b30ad4ab5090af7/buds/06.md)

### **Key Features of BUD-06:**

- `HEAD /upload`: This endpoint allows clients to validate if an upload can be completed before sending the blob to the server. It verifies the blob's hash, size, and MIME type through the `X-SHA-256`, `X-Content-Type`, and `X-Content-Length` headers, returning a custom header `X-Upload-Message` with information about the upload feasibility.
  
This prevents unnecessary traffic by rejecting files based on their hash, size, MIME type, or other server-specific conditions, ensuring that only valid uploads are processed.

### **Headers introduced:**

- `X-SHA-256`: SHA-256 hash of the blob.
- `X-Content-Length`: The size of the blob in bytes.
- `X-Content-Type`: The MIME type of the blob (e.g. `application/pdf`).
- `X-Upload-Message`: A human-readable message explaining why the upload cannot proceed.

### Why Custom Headers for `X-Content-Length` and `X-Content-Type`

Custom headers like `X-Content-Length` and `X-Content-Type` are used because many servers, including Node.js, do not handle the standard `Content-Length` and `Content-Type` headers correctly with the HEAD method. Since HEAD requests often omit or mishandle these headers, we ensure consistency by using custom headers that work reliably across different server implementations.

### **Examples:**

Example request from the client:
```http
X-Content-Type: application/pdf
X-Content-Length: 184292
X-SHA-256: 88a74d0b866c8ba79251a11fe5ac807839226870e77355f02eaf68b156522576
```

Example response if the upload can be done:
```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

If the upload cannot proceed, the server `MUST` return an appropriate HTTP status code and a custom header `X-Upload-Message` with a human readable error message.

Some examples of error messages:

```http
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
X-Upload-Message: Invalid X-SHA-256 header format.
```

```http
HTTP/1.1 413 Content Too Large
X-Upload-Message: File too large. Max allowed size is 100MB
```

```http
HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type
X-Upload-Message: Unsupported file type.
```

title: HEAD /Upload + BUD-06 Payment storage
body:
This pull request introduces enhancements to the BUD-02 specification that maintain backward compatibility with existing servers while addressing new use cases.

1. **Introduction of Header-Based Upload Information Request (`HEAD /upload`)**:
  - New `HEAD /upload` endpoint that uses the `Blossom-Content-Type`, `Blossom-Content-Length`, and `Digest` headers to obtain the MIME type, size, and hash of the blob that will be uploaded, returning an HTTP status code and a custom header `Blossom-Upload-Message` to indicate whether the upload can be performed or not.

   - This endpioint reduces unnecessary data transfer and allows clients to quickly determine the feasibility of uploading a file based on its size and type.

Example request headers from the client:

  ```
  Blossom-Content-Type: application/pdf
  Blossom-Content-Length: 184292
  ```
Example response headers from the server if the upload is allowed:

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
If the upload is not allowed, the server MUST return an appropriate HTTP status code and a custom header `Blossom-Upload-Message` with a human readable error message.

Example for not allowed upload:

```http
HTTP/1.1 413 Forbidden
Blossom-Upload-Message: File too large. Max allowed size is 100MB
```

2. **BUD-06 Payment storage**

   - The specification now includes a provision where servers may require payment for storage. In such cases, the server responds with a `402 Payment Required` status code and 'Www-Authenticate' with the macaroon and the payment request fields using [L402 protocol](https://l402.org/) standard.
     
     - **Client-Side Handling**: For clients that do understand the 'Www-Authenticate' header, they can display the invoice and facilitate payment directly, ensuring a seamless upload process once payment is completed using L402 standard.
     
     - **Example**:
    ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6eed7e99-453a-4e9c-a3bc-546b5665ebf8)
    ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90284bdf-a3db-43f3-90bf-4ded3423d134)


    
     - **Backward Compatibility**: Existing clients that do not interpret the `Www-Authenticate` header will receive the expected HTTP status code (402) and can handle the response accordingly. The server will not disrupt the interaction with such clients, maintaining a consistent user experience.
     
     - **Example**
      Here is an example of a QR code generated by nostrcheck-server for the `url` field as long as a payment has not been made:
      
      ![QR Code Example](https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/assets/125748180/87e52a69-9ac8-4d53-9e1a-6af4e1cae086)

title: Allow authorization events to include multiple x tags

This would allow clients to use a single authorization event for multiple `PUT /upload` or `DELETE /<sha256>` requests

**When multiple `x` tags are present on an authorization event sent to the `DELETE /<sha256>` or `PUT /mirror` endpoints, it MUST NOT be interpreted as a bulk delete or bulk mirror**

title: Fix a spelling mistake in BUD-01
Restrict get authorization event to a single blob or server
body:
This PR restricts the `GET /<sha256>` authorization to either a single blob sha256 or a single server.

It does this by requiring the get authorization event to either have a `x` tag with the sha256 ( `["x","b1674191a88ec5cdd733e4240a81803105dc412d6c6708d53ab94fc248f4f553"]` ) or a `server` tag with the servers URL ( `["server", "https://cdn.example.com/"]` )

This prevents malicious servers from reusing get auth events to impersonate the user with other servers

Example:
Server `A` and `B` both require authorization to read blobs
User creates an authorization event to read blobs and sends it to `B` to retrieve a single blob
Server `B` returns the blob but is malicious and reuses the users authorization event to talk to server `A` as the user to retrieve other blobs

title: Add requirement for sha256 on upload
body:
Replace the requirement for the `size` tag with an `x` tag containing the sha256 hash of the blob being uploaded

This is much more secure and removes the possibility of an attacker using another users "upload authorization" event with a padded blob
